collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 24 major government space agencies enumerated in the Wikipedia 'List of government space agencies' Table[4] (the launch-related capabilities subset table within the master article — 24 agencies with at least an entry in the launch-capabilities table). For each agency the staged row records the Full Name (full English agency name), Country or Organization (sovereign-state or intergovernmental sponsor), and Founded (4-digit integer year of the current named entity). The 24-row universe is fully source-defined via Table[4]'s membership rather than a curator-derived 'major agencies' filter. The schema is designed for benchmark evaluation: all 4 cells are exact-match-evaluable; Agency is the PK lookup target (acronym for most rows; full name for Iranian Space Agency and Israel Space Agency to avoid PK collision on shared acronym 'ISA'); Full Name is exact-match text; Country or Organization is exact-match from a 24-distinct-value vocabulary; Founded is exact-match numeric integer year.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (List_of_government_space_agencies): universe + filter + value (defines the master Table[3] 89-row enumeration AND the Table[4] 24-row launch-related capabilities subset that defines the universe; supplies the per-row Agency identifier verbatim from Table[4]'s Agency column with footnote refs stripped, Full Name verbatim from Table[3]'s Name column cross-referenced by acronym, Country or Organization from Table[3]'s Country column with ESA member-state normalization, and Founded as the 4-digit integer year extracted from Table[3]'s Founded column corresponding to the current named entity).

Single-source Tier B instance. The Wikipedia master article is the canonical authoritative compilation of government space agencies AND their launch capabilities. Per-row cells: Agency identifier is from Table[4]'s Agency column; Full Name, Country, and Founded are cross-referenced from Table[3]'s master rows by acronym/name match. Cell-level audit can spot-check any of the 24 rows against the master article's Table[3] and Table[4]; no per-agency article fetches are needed because all 4 staged cells are derivable from the two tables within the single source URL. Notable cross-ref subtleties documented in normalization_decisions: (i) Two rows where Table[4] disambiguates by full name rather than acronym to avoid PK collision (Iranian Space Agency and Israel Space Agency both have acronym 'ISA' per Table[3]); (ii) one row where Table[4] uses 'MSA' as acronym but Table[3] master uses 'AEM' for the same Mexican Space Agency (cross-ref by row position and country flag); (iii) the ESA row where Table[3]'s Country cell concatenates 22 member states (normalized to 'European Space Agency member states' for the staged cell).
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (24 major government space agencies — the Table[4] launch-related capabilities subset within the master Wikipedia article) is fully source-defined via Table[4]'s membership; per-row attribute cells are verbatim/lightly-normalized from Table[3] master via acronym cross-ref. Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical major agencies (NASA, ESA, JAXA, ISRO, CNSA, Roscosmos); mid-difficulty cells include the well-known but less-headline-grabbing agencies (CNES France, ASI Italy, CSA Canada, KARI South Korea); harder calibration cells include the more obscure or recently-founded agencies (CONAE Argentina, SUPARCO Pakistan, SSAU Ukraine, NATA North Korea, MSA Mexico). Row count (24) clears the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected from the picker's recommended factual_lookup gap-1-saturator candidate slate (world's tallest dams — taken by parallel agent; major space agencies — this instance; major straits of the world). Picker rationale: extends the under-represented organizations bucket from 2 (universities, companies) to 3 with a NEW space-agencies fine-class.
- Category: factual_lookup (gap 1 before this staging — 4 of 5 with eu_member_states_accession_years, chemical_elements_discovered_1869_1945, twelve_olympians_greek_to_roman, oceanic_trenches_named_deeps; this instance brings factual_lookup to 5/5 SATURATING the category — FIFTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5) primary; geographic (gap 3) secondary because the Country or Organization column provides a geographic axis. Per references/artifact-contract.md, factual_lookup pairs canonically with operation_type=projection (when the schema is a multi-attribute SELECT over a fixed entity universe); the db_analog 'SELECT agency, full_name, country_or_organization, founded FROM government_space_agencies WHERE agency_in_launch_related_capabilities_table = TRUE ORDER BY agency' is the canonical factual-lookup-with-source-defined-filter primitive.
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, single source URL; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 1 (master 'List of government space agencies' article supplies both Table[3] master and Table[4] launch-capable subset).
- Expected shape: 24 rows × 4 columns; PK = Agency.
- Domain: Science/Space Exploration — extends the existing Space Exploration subdomain from 3 event-keyed instances (crewed_spaceflight_fatal_incidents, apollo_lunar_landing_mission_crews, notable_robotic_spacecraft_missions) to 4 instances. Mirrors the EdTech pattern (major_b2c_online_learning_platforms uses Education/EdTech domain with organizations/companies entity class — topic-as-domain, organization-as-entity). Per domain_taxonomy.md, the Space Exploration subdomain is appropriate for organizations whose purpose is space exploration.
- Entity class: organizations/space-agencies — NEW fine-class within the under-represented organizations bucket (bucket count 2 → 3, joining universities and companies). Entity-class novelty axis score: strong (NEW fine-class within under-represented bucket per the 4-axis selection rubric).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) Two rows use full-name Agency PK instead of acronym to avoid PK collision: Iran and Israel both have acronym 'ISA' per Table[3], and Table[4] disambiguates by using the full name as the Agency identifier. The staged values preserve this convention. (b) The ESA row's Country cell in Table[3] is a comma-separated 22-member-state list; the staged value normalizes to 'European Space Agency member states' for the closed-vocab Country cell. (c) The Soviet space program row is staged with the † defunct-marker per the source — including defunct entities is consistent with epidemics instance precedent (ongoing + historical events both in scope). (d) All 24 Table[4] members are retained per source-defined membership rather than any capability-based filter; the staged schema does not include the launch-capability columns, so their values are not staged answer cells. (Note: pandas.read_html parses some Table[4] capability cells as NaN because the source uses flag/check icons rather than literal text — the source visibly shows Yes/No markers for CSA, MSA, POLSA, UKSA, etc.; the universe-membership rule does not depend on these markers.) (e) Acronym discrepancy between Table[3] and Table[4] for Mexican Space Agency: Table[3] master uses 'AEM' but Table[4] launch-capable subset uses 'MSA'; the staged Agency value follows Table[4] (the universe-defining table) per the precedent established for cycle-2 audit interactions. (f) Founded year extraction for multi-year founding-history cells uses the year corresponding to the current named entity (e.g., 'CONAE' year 1991 not 1961 CNIE predecessor year).
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets space agencies or organizations whose purpose is space exploration.

Why 'Table[4] launch-related capabilities subset' universe rather than alternatives: deep-dive on universe design considered 4 options. Option A (Table[3] full 89-row master) would include many obscure recent agencies (Mauritius, Costa Rica, Bahrain, etc.) with low LLM-knowability and excessive row count. Option B (Table[4] 24-row launch-capable subset, the chosen design) is the source-defined 'major' subset — agencies with at least an entry in the launch-related capabilities table. Option C (filter by 'First space traveler' capability = 45 agencies) would broaden too much by including collaboration-only entries. Option D (Table[5] 7-row deep-space subset) fails the 10-row gate. Option B was selected as the cleanest balance of source-defined-rigor + manageable size.

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: factual_lookup pairs reasonably with operation_type=projection per references/artifact-contract.md. The 3-attribute SELECT per row (Full Name + Country + Founded) over the source-defined entity universe is the canonical factual-lookup-with-multi-attribute primitive (matching twelve_olympians_greek_to_roman's 4-col SELECT pattern and oceanic_trenches_named_deeps's 4-col composite-PK pattern).

Adding an organization-keyed instance to Space Exploration diversifies the subdomain's entity-class mix. Mirrors the EdTech pattern where major_b2c_online_learning_platforms uses Education/EdTech domain with organizations/companies entity class.

Entity class selection: organizations/space-agencies — NEW fine-class within the organizations bucket. The bucket was at 2 instances before this staging (universities via aau_big_ten_intersection_universities; companies via major_b2c_online_learning_platforms); this instance brings it to 3. NEW fine-class scores strong on the Entity-class novelty axis per the 4-axis selection rubric introduced 2026-05-14.

Claim type: source_defined — the universe is fully defined by Table[4]'s membership in the master article. The curator does NOT supplement the universe with non-Table[4] agencies. All 4 staged cells are derivable from the master article (Table[3] + Table[4]) with only mechanical normalization (footnote-ref stripping, ESA member-state list normalization, Founded year extraction from multi-year cells).

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 1): cycle-1 audit verdict 'Ready' — 0 BLOCKING, 2 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. The data itself is source-faithful (24 rows match Table[4] membership exactly; Iran/Israel disambiguation accepted; MSA/AEM cross-table discrepancy documented as Table[4]-following; CSA Canada/Chile resolution accepted; Soviet † defunct entity accepted; ESA member-state normalization accepted; Founded-year spot-checks all passed). Both hygiene items addressed in this cycle-1 repair pass: (a) HYGIENE #1 (factual) — current-state prose misstated four Table[4] rows (CSA-Canadian, MSA-Mexican, POLSA, UKSA) as having all-NaN launch capabilities or no demonstrated launch capabilities yet. The source's Launch capability table actually shows Yes/No markers via flag/check icons for these rows (e.g., CSA Canada: Yes/Yes/No/No/No; UKSA: Yes/Yes/Yes/No/No); pandas.read_html parses these as NaN because the markers are images rather than literal text. The prose inference 'no demonstrated launch capabilities' was wrong. Resolved by rewriting the relevant prose sentences in temporal_note, _extraction_notes (Risks/adaptation (d) bullet), decision_log Risks/adaptation (d) bullet, normalization_decisions universe-definition prose, and open_questions #3 to: (i) reaffirm Table[4]-membership-alone as the universe rule (not capability-derived); (ii) explicitly note the pandas-icon-parsing artifact that produces NaN cells without changing the source's visible Yes/No markers; (iii) drop the 'no demonstrated launch capabilities' framing. Resolved by rewriting the decade-distribution sentence to: 1950s 2 (NASA 1958, Soviet 1955), 1960s 3 (CNES 1961, ISRO 1969, SUPARCO 1961), 1970s 2 (ESA 1975, SNSA 1972), 1980s 4 (Israel 1983, ASI 1988, CSA 1989, KARI 1989), 1990s 5 (CONAE 1991, Roscosmos 1992, SSAU 1992, CNSA 1993, AEB 1994), 2000s 2 (JAXA 2003, Iranian Space Agency 2004), 2010s 5 (MSA 2010, UKSA 2010, POLSA 2014, NZSA 2016, ASA 2018), 2020s 1 (NATA 2023) — sum = 24. Net cycle-1 changes: 5 prose-section scrubs across draft.json and curation.json on the capability-NaN-misclaim wording; 1 _extraction_notes Founded-distribution rewrite; no CSV / source_count / row count / schema / column changes (still 24 rows × 4 cols, source_count 1, Agency PK unique, alphabetical sort intact).

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 2): cycle-2 verification audit verdict 'Ready+Clean' — 0 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. Both cycle-1 hygiene items confirmed resolved (capability-NaN-misclaim wording cleared from current-state prose; Founded-year decade distribution correctly sums to 24); historical cycle-1 paragraph legitimately retains the OLD wording for narrative fidelity; 24-row CSV / schema / source_count / preflight all still pass. The cited source still supports the launch-capability table framing including Yes/No icon-marker rows for CSA/MSA/POLSA/UKSA. Instance marked accept-ready as of 2026-05-14. Total cycle count: 3 (cycle-0 staging + cycles 1-2 audit/repair). Universe stable at 24 events across all cycles; both repairs were prose-only narrative-alignment scrubs (no CSV/schema/source-set changes). The instance SATURATES `factual_lookup` at 5/5 — **FIFTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR** after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5. Useful reference: single-source factual_lookup instances with sub-table-defined-universe (Table[4] within a master article) require explicit documentation that the staged schema does NOT include the sub-table's filter columns (here, the 5 launch-capability columns); the prose-pitfall is inferring 'no capability demonstrated' from pandas-parsed NaN cells when the source actually renders the capability via flag/check icons.
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is the 24 government space agencies enumerated in the Wikipedia 'List of government space agencies' master article's Table[4] (per pandas.read_html — the launch-related capabilities subset table with columns Agency / Operates launch site / Suborbital launch capable / Orbital launch capable / Cryogenic rocket engine use / Reusable systems use). Table[4] membership alone is the source-defined 'major space agencies' subset — the 5 launch-capability columns in Table[4] are not staged answer columns and are not used to filter the universe in either direction. (Note: pandas.read_html parses some of Table[4]'s capability cells as NaN because the source renders Yes/No markers via flag/check icons rather than literal text strings; the source visibly shows Yes/No markers for the rows whose pandas-parsed cells are NaN.) The 24 members are: CONAE (Argentina), ASA (Australia), AEB (Brazil), CSA (Canada), CNSA (China), ESA (European member states), CNES (France), ISRO (India), Iranian Space Agency (Iran), Israel Space Agency (Israel), ASI (Italy), JAXA (Japan), NATA (North Korea), KARI (South Korea), MSA (Mexico), NZSA (New Zealand), SUPARCO (Pakistan), POLSA (Poland), Roscosmos (Russia), Soviet space program † (Soviet Union, defunct), SNSA (Sweden), SSAU (Ukraine), UKSA (United Kingdom), NASA (United States). Agency identifier normalization: each row's Agency is taken verbatim from Table[4]'s Agency column with footnote references (e.g., '[2]', '[100]', '[117]') stripped. For 22 of 24 rows the Agency value is the agency's standard acronym (NASA, ESA, JAXA, etc.). For 2 rows where Table[4] would have a PK collision on the acronym 'ISA' (shared by Iranian Space Agency per Table[3] row 31 and Israel Space Agency per Table[3] row 32), Table[4] disambiguates by using the full English name as the Agency identifier; the staged Agency value preserves this convention. Full Name normalization: each row's Full Name is taken verbatim from Table[3]'s Name column (cross-referenced by acronym match or by Table[4]-row-to-Table[3]-row positional alignment). For the two Iran/Israel rows where the Agency value is already the full name, the Full Name column repeats the same value (acknowledged redundancy preserving source structure). Country or Organization normalization: each row's Country is taken verbatim from Table[3]'s Country column, with one normalization rule: (i) the ESA row's Country cell in Table[3] is a comma-separated list of 22 European member states ('Austria  Belgium  Czech Republic  Denmark  Estonia  Finland  France  Germany  Greece  Hungary  Ireland  Italy  Luxembourg  Netherlands  Norway  Portugal  Poland Romania  Spain  Sweden  Switzerland  United Kingdom'); the staged value normalizes this to the descriptive label 'European Space Agency member states' for the closed-vocab Country cell. The Soviet space program row's Country cell is staged as 'Soviet Union †' per Table[3]'s row 63 with the defunct-marker preserved. All other 22 rows take Country verbatim from Table[3]. One cross-table acronym discrepancy: Table[3] master uses 'AEM' for Mexican Space Agency (row 44, founded 30 Jul 2010) but Table[4] launch-capable subset uses 'MSA' for the same agency (identified by the flag-of-Mexico image adjacent to 'MSA' in the source HTML); the staged Agency value follows Table[4]'s 'MSA' since Table[4] is the universe-defining table. Founded normalization: each row's Founded is the 4-digit integer year extracted from Table[3]'s Founded column, using the year corresponding to the CURRENT named entity in multi-year founding-history cells. Examples: 'CONAE' = 1991 from '1961 (CNIE) 28 May 1991 (CONAE)'; 'ASA' = 2018 from '1986 (NSP) 1 Jul 2018 (ASA)'; 'ESA' = 1975 from '1964 (ESRO/ELDO) 30 May 1975 (ESA)'; 'ISRO' = 1969 from '1962 (INCOSPAR) 15th Aug 1969 (ISRO)'; 'NATA' = 2023 from '1980s (KCST) 2013 (NADA) 2023 (NATA)'; 'POLSA' = 2014 from '29 Sep 1976 (CBK PAN) 26 Sep 2014 (POLSA)'; 'NASA' = 1958 from '29 Jul 1958'; 'Soviet space program' = 1955 founding year from '1955 disbanded 25 Dec 1991'. Sort order: the CSV is sorted **alphabetically by Agency identifier ascending** (benchmark default for factual_lookup-category single-PK lookup tables). Sort produces AEB / ASA / ASI / CNES / CNSA / CONAE / CSA / ESA / ISRO / Iranian Space Agency / Israel Space Agency / JAXA / KARI / MSA / NASA / NATA / NZSA / POLSA / Roscosmos / SNSA / SSAU / SUPARCO / Soviet space program † / UKSA. The two full-name-PK rows (Iranian/Israel) sort by their full-name strings; the Soviet space program † row sorts after SUPARCO due to lowercase-letter codepoint ordering ('Sov' > 'SUP' because 'o' codepoint > 'U' codepoint in Python's default string sort).
open_questions: 1. Whether the Iran and Israel rows should use full-name Agency PK (current staging, per Table[4] disambiguation convention) or whether the acronym 'ISA' should be staged with composite PK (Agency, Country) to disambiguate. Current staging uses full-name per source's Table[4]. 2. Whether the Mexican Space Agency row's Agency identifier should be 'MSA' (Table[4]) or 'AEM' (Table[3] master). The two source tables disagree; current staging uses 'MSA' per Table[4]'s membership-defining role. 3. Whether the universe should be further restricted by a curator-derived launch-capability filter beyond Table[4]-membership. Current staging retains all 24 Table[4] members per source-defined membership; the staged schema does not include the launch-capability columns so their values are not staged answer cells. 4. Whether the Soviet space program † row should be retained as defunct entity (current staging) or dropped to focus on currently-active agencies (would reduce universe to 23 rows). 5. Whether Founded year for multi-year founding-history cells should use the current-entity year (current staging) or the earliest-predecessor year (e.g., CONAE = 1961 CNIE instead of 1991 CONAE; ISRO = 1962 INCOSPAR instead of 1969 ISRO). 6. Whether the ESA row's Country cell should be normalized to 'European Space Agency member states' (current staging) or preserve the 22-member-state list verbatim (would create a multi-line cell). 7. Whether a Headquarters column should be added (5-col schema instead of 4-col) — would require per-agency Wikipedia article fetches (source_count 1 → ~25). 8. Whether the Founded cell for Roscosmos should be 1992 (post-Soviet establishment of Roscosmos) or include the Russian Federal Space Agency's later renaming dates. Current staging uses 1992 per Table[3]'s '25 Feb 1992' cell.
